newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak SAX index unchanged despite blue chip gains.
newsitem.headline: Slovak SAX index unchanged despite blue chip gains.

text.p: Major Slovak shares closed mostly up in moderate trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Tuesday, but losses to several minor issues left the SAX index unchanged at 167.43 points
Brokers said the market may have registerd higher activity, but they did not expect any significant moves in either directon in near future.
"We can see higher interest in several issues due to attractive prices, but those who hold the shares seem not yet accepting lower levels," said Libor Briska of Creditanstalt.

Oil refiner Slovnaft posted the heaviest gains among the blue chips, closing up 40 crowns at 750 crowns. But brokers said that insignificant volume of traded stocks could not show a longer-term increase.
"Furthermore, you cannot find larger packages of Slovnaft shares for such a high price at the moment," Briska said.
Steel producer VSZ closed up 19 crowns at 499, but its average price - used for calculating the index - eased by 4.17 percent and help equalised gains to other blue chips.
Brokers said they considered a VSZ share price at around 500 crowns as a fair market value of the stock.

Oil and gas storage company Nafta closed up 13 crowns at 1,373, but traded only 17 shares, which, brokers said, demonstrated the wait-and-see attitude to the issue ahead of extraordinary shareholdres meeting scheduled for Wednesday.

The EGM is due to approve the company's investment plans and dealers said the market could learn a lot about the little-known new owners of Nafta and their strategy with the firm from the approved plans.

Overall volume rose to 564,681 shares, boosted mainly by direct sales, from 126,530 stocks traded on Monday. The turnover increased to 324.83 million crowns, from 38.38 million on Monday. -- Peter Laca, Bratislava Newsroom, 42-7-563-3687
